newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power firm despite plant returns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power firm despite plant returns.

text.p: Spot physical electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. were firm Tuesday compared to Monday's levels despite scheduled returns of several regional nuclear plants from refueling.

More than 2,600 megawatts are expected to resume service starting later this week: 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear unit in Berwick, Pa.; 610 MW Oyster Creek nuclear station in Forked River, N.J.; and 833 MW Beaver Valley 2 nuclear unit in Shippingport, Pa.

In addition to more generating capacity coming back, spot power values in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool remained strong amid relatively mild autumn weather in the region.
"Loads are down...This is a shoulder month," said a PJM trader surprised by the strength in prices.
Some participants cited slightly reduced output from two PECO Energy operated nuclear power units as supportive factors for daily PJM prices.
The 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peach Bottom 2 nuclear unit in Delta, Pa., was running at 64 percent capacity late Monday due to adjustment of the reactor's control rods.
The 1,055 MW Limerick 2 nuclear unit's output was trimmed to 73 percent of capacity to work a vibration problem in a condensate pump.
PECO was not available for comment, but industry sources said both Pennsylvania nuclear power plants were planned to resume full output late today or early Wednesday.
Firm, peak PJM electricity prices for Wednesday delivery were quoted $23.25-$23.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Monday's deals done mostly in the $22.50-$23.35 range.
Next-week firm, peak PJM power was quoted at $22.50-$23.50.
PJM electricity for the rest of October was pegged at $21.50-$22.25, weaker than Monday's $22.00-$23.00.
November PJM electricity was assessed at $22.90-$23.20, up from a quote of $22.65-$22.75 on Monday.
December PJM power was discussed at $26.90-$27.00, better bid than Monday's $26.75-$27.00.
For the rest of the 1996 fourth quarter, PJM electricity was talked at $24.10-$24.40, higher than Monday's range of $23.75-$24.00.
January/February 1997 PJM power was pegged near $30.75, compared with Monday's $30.45-$30.75 range.
First-quarter 1997 PJM was again quoted at $28.15-$28.50 and second quarter 1997 PJM deliveries $21.75-$22.25.
